newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: FORECAST - Renong profits seen sharply up.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST - Renong profits seen sharply up.

text.p: Malaysian conglomerate Renong Bhd is expected to announce a sharp increase of between 73.2 and 87.7 percent in net profit when full-year results are released later on Thursday, analysts said.
The analysts forecast net profit of between 360 million to 390 million ringgit for the year ended June 30, 1996, against 207.8 million in the previous year.
According to The Estimate Directory of analysts' forecasts, a poll of 30 houses expects Renong's net profit at an average 365.4 million ringgit.
They said major contributors to profits will be Prolink Development Sdn Bhd, a 64 percent subsidiary that is developing a huge township in southern Johor state.
Renong's flagship, United Engineers (M) Bhd is also expected to boost group earnings, they said.
United Engineers owns Projek Lebuhraya Utara-Selatan (PLUS), toll operator of the 900 kilometre North-South expressway in peninsular Malaysia.
"A big contribution will come from Prolink, which have booked in profits from the sale of a few parcels of land in Gelang Patah," said an analyst with a British brokerage.
He projected Renong's net profit for the 1995/96 financial year at 373 million ringgit, with Prolink contributing about 130 million.
Prolink has about 10,000 hectares of land in Gelang Patah district in Johor that will be developed over 25 to 30 years.
Analysts said Prolink and United Engineers will be the driving forces behind Renong's growth, as flat performances are expected from its other subsidiaries and associate companies.
"I don't think there will be many surprises from the companies in the group," said an analyst with a local brokerage.
The sprawling conglomerate has interests in more than a dozen listed companies involved in construction, hotel services, telecommunications, transport, finance and oil and gas.
HLG Securities, which forecast a net profit of 387.8 million ringgit, recommended a long-term buy on Renong stock.
"The share price has fallen over the past few weeks, so valuations are on a much more comfortable level," it said in a report to clients on Wednesday.
Renong shares were trading at 3.86 ringgit at midday on Thursday, down four cents from Wednesday.
